question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to agent-core, and should that be a new mode/config surface or a change to current `parallel` semantics?
rationale: The source-level performance opportunity is clear, but the change affects core runtime ordering and safety semantics rather than repairing a broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for execute-on-parse behavior with transcript, hook, approval, cancellation, and ordering tests.

options.title: Backlog Performance Idea
options.body: Keep the issue as a performance backlog item until maintainers decide the API and compatibility policy.

options.title: Reject Early Dispatch
options.body: Close or defer the request if maintainers want post-stream batch execution to remain the only supported concurrency model.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for execute-on-parse behavior with transcript, hook, approval, cancellation, and ordering tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history puts the packaged agent loop, stream parser, and runtime parameter surfaces under this contributor's current-main work.
